identity.libraryClass: statsforecast.models.CrostonClassic (or hand-rolled paired-SES, ~40 LOC) — IMPLEMENTATION SOURCE UNRESOLVED
identity.description: The intermittent-demand specialist: runs two separate exponential smoothers — one on non-zero demand SIZES, one on the INTERVALS between demand events — and forecasts the flat demand rate size/interval. Its niche is sparse series full of zeros (event registrations, per-chapter merch orders, low-volume renewals) where every mainstream forecaster smears the zeros into nonsense.

consumes.note: non-negative demand series on a regular grid where zeros are DATA (no demand that period), not missing values — the defining input regime

emits.note: a FLAT mean demand rate over the horizon (size-level / interval-level) — a rate to feed inventory/capacity math, not a varying path; no native intervals

alpha.note: shared smoothing rate for both the size and interval smoothers; classic Croston fixes it at 0.1, the 'optimized' variant fits it

variant.note: sba applies the Syntetos-Boylan (1 - alpha/2) bias correction; optimized fits alpha per smoother

invariances.why: smoothing demand sizes is equivariant to rescaling them; intervals are unitless counts and unaffected
any transform that moves zeros (log is undefined at 0) destroys the zero/non-zero partition the method is built on — transforms are actively destructive here
needs a regular grid to count inter-demand intervals; a genuinely missing period is ambiguous between 'no demand' (a zero) and 'unobserved' and must be resolved before fitting
single numeric demand series; no exogenous pathway
assumes demand sizes and inter-demand intervals are independent processes — the known premise whose violation biases classic Croston and motivates the SBA correction
what matters is the COUNT of non-zero demand events, not raw series length — a long series with 4 events still cannot identify two smoothers
forecasts beyond observed time, but only as a FLAT demand rate — no trend or seasonal extrapolation exists in the mechanism at all

featureStats.why: the routing stat: high zero share is precisely the regime where mean/recursion forecasters fail and Croston's size/interval split earns its keep
ADI is one axis of the Syntetos-Boylan quadrant that separates smooth, intermittent, erratic, and lumpy demand — it decides Croston vs a plain smoother
the other Syntetos-Boylan axis: high size variability (lumpy demand) is where classic Croston's bias grows and the SBA variant should be preferred
the effective sample size — two smoothers are unidentifiable from a handful of demand events regardless of series length

modelMetrics.why: the family scoreboard still applies — MASE's in-sample naive scaling stays defined under many zeros where percentage errors divide by zero and collapse

edgeCases.behavior: degenerates to SES with pointless interval machinery
edgeCases.note: route to ets/sma via the zero_fraction stat

edgeCases.behavior: size and interval smoothers have nothing to fit; rate undefined
flat-rate forecast is systematically wrong — the mechanism cannot represent either
edgeCases.note: seasonal-intermittent series need aggregation or a different method

edgeCases.behavior: smoothers pinned to initial values; forecast is folklore

driver.constructor: CrostonClassic()/CrostonSBA()/CrostonOptimized().fit(y) via statsforecast — OR hand-rolled paired SES on (sizes, intervals); UNCERTAINTY: statsmodels has no Croston, so the driver either takes the statsforecast dep for one niche method or hand-rolls ~40 LOC — unresolved, flagged for the driver tranche decision
deps: statsforecast>=1.7 (UNCERTAIN — may be dropped in favor of a hand-rolled implementation to avoid a whole dep for one method)
driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter: (time_col, value_col, freq, horizon); missing-period policy resolved to explicit zeros BEFORE fit; flat rate tiled across the horizon

placementClaims.why: the grid must be regular, but missing demand periods are filled with ZERO (no demand), never interpolated — interpolation fabricates demand events and corrupts both smoothers
log/Box-Cox are undefined or distorting at zero and dissolve the zero/non-zero partition that defines intermittency
scale-equivariant on sizes; intervals are counts
single numeric series has nothing to encode
